report.answer: During tree matching, when the walk in node.getValue (tree.go:418) reaches a wildChild whose nType is `param` (a `:name` segment), it scans path bytes until the next '/' or end-of-string (tree.go ~487-490), then stores a Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: path[:end]} into value.params/Params (tree.go ~490-513), stripping the leading ':' from the node's stored path to get the key name; a `catchAll` (`*name`) node instead captures the entire remaining path in one shot (Key: n.path[2:], stripping '/*') and immediately returns. Params is a preallocated []Param slice passed down from Context.params via engine.allocateContext (sized by engine.maxParams, set during addRoute/countParams), so capture is allocation-free on the hot path; a skippedNodes backtracking stack (tree.go skippedNode struct) allows the walker to retry static branches before falling back to a wildcard match.

verified.summary: param-type wildcard node captures a single path segment as Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: path[:end]} where end is the next '/' or path end
catchAll-type wildcard node captures the entire remaining path as Param{Key: n.path[2:], Value: path} and returns immediately
Params slice is preallocated/grown by capacity (globalParamsCount) rather than appended, avoiding heap allocation during matching
verified.evidence: tree.go getValue param/catchAll cases, 'Preallocate capacity if necessary' blocks

verified.summary: Matched params are optionally unescaped via url.QueryUnescape when unescape=true (engine.UnescapePathValues)
verified.evidence: tree.go getValue, val/path unescape branches in param and catchAll cases

verified.summary: handleHTTPRequest passes c.params (from context, sized via engine.maxParams) into root.getValue and assigns the result to c.Params

relevantFiles.reason: getValue (param/catchAll cases) is where :name and *catchall params are captured during matching
handleHTTPRequest supplies c.params and consumes value.params/c.Params after matching
